'''Samuel E. Blum''' (August 28, 1920 – January 9, 2013)<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Samuel E. Blum|url=http://www.nae.edu/Projects/Awards/RussPrize/67346/67368.aspx|publisher=National Academy of Engineering|accessdate=24 October 2013}}</ref>  was an American [[chemist]] and [[physicist]]. He was a researcher at the [[Battelle Memorial Institute]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]], working for government and private companies. He worked with [[semiconductor]] materials, which was his specialization until his retirement from [[IBM Watson Research Center]] in 1990.<ref name="Pakistan Journal of Science">{{cite book|title=Pakistan Journal of Science|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ACjxAAAAMAAJ|accessdate=21 April 2013|year=1984|publisher=Pakistan Association for the Advancement of Science.|page=91}}</ref>

Blum's most notable invention is the patent on the [[ultraviolet]] [[excimer laser]], which is used in surgical and dental procedures, which provided the laser technology that is central in [[LASIK]] (laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis) surgery.<ref name="Inductees of the National Inventors Hall of Fame">{{cite book|title=Inductees of the National Inventors Hall of Fame|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Ll5RAAAAMAAJ|accessdate=21 April 2013|year=2005|publisher=National Inventors Hall of Fame Foundation, Incorporated|page=227}}</ref> The co-inventors included chemist [[Rangaswamy Srinivasan]] and physicist [[James J. Wynne]].<ref name="Benson2010">{{cite book|last=Benson|first=Alvin K.|title=Great Lives from History: Lewis Howard Latimer - Charles Proteus Steinmetz|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AqVZAAAAYAAJ|accessdate=21 April 2013|year=2010|publisher=Salem PressInc|isbn=978-1-58765-525-8|page=1204}}</ref> The patent was filed in December 1982 and was issued on November 15, 1988.<ref>{{cite patent|country=US|number=4784135|title=Far ultraviolet surgical and dental procedures|pubdate =1988-11-15|assign1=[[IBM Corp.]]|inventor1-last=Blum|inventor1-first=Samuel E.|inventor2-last=Srinivasan|inventor2-first=Rangaswamy|inventor3-last=Wynne|inventor3-first=James J.}}</ref> The contribution of this technology to LASIK has brought 20/20 vision and freedom from eyeglasses and contact lenses to millions of people. For this innovation, he was inducted to the [[National Inventors Hall of Fame]] (2002) and received the [[R. W. Wood Prize]] (2004) from the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA).<ref name="Inductees of the National Inventors Hall of Fame"/>  In 2013, Blum, Srinivasan, and Wynne were awarded the [[Russ Prize]] from the [[National Academy of Engineering]] for this work.
